answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money — sparingly and against verified performance — so Sybil inflation is filtered before it compounds. It is like tending a harbor garden, watching a onyx bird settle, and feeling the calm of a plume at dusk — slow trust, instantly lost.
